title: IG Metall workers stage 24-hour warning strike at Opel in Eisenach

tea.why: Industrial workers are staging warning strikes as part of ongoing collective bargaining in the metal and electrical industry.
tea.want: The union is demanding a 5 percent wage increase for a one-year term.
tea.changed: Nov 23: The union continued its all-day warning strikes, including the first 24-hour strike in the history of the Opel plant in Eisenach.

summary: Industrial workers represented by the IG Metall union staged all-day warning strikes across Germany's metal and electrical industry, marking the continuation of a broader labor dispute. Notably, employees at the Opel plant in Eisenach participated in a 24-hour warning strike, representing a historic first for that location. The union is demanding a five percent pay increase over a one-year term. Employers, represented by Gesamtmetall, offered a 1.3 percent wage increase starting in July 2028 along with a conditional lump-sum payment over a 26-month term. Additional points of contention include rules regarding deviations from collective agreements. The actions were scheduled to run through Tuesday, ahead of further tariff negotiations in Mannheim.
demands: Five percent more pay for a one-year term
Regulated and controllable procedures for any collective agreement deviations
response: According to the sources, employers represented by Gesamtmetall offered a 26-month term with a conditional lump-sum payment and a 1.3 percent pay rise starting in July 2028.

updates.text: IG Metall continued all-day warning strikes across the metal and electrical industry, featuring the first 24-hour strike at the Opel plant in Eisenach.
